title: FERC Directs Nation's Largest Grid Operator to Create New Rules to Embrace Innovation and Protect Consumers (Order on PJM Co-location and Behind-the-Meter Generation)
key_claim: On 18 December 2025 FERC ordered PJM to develop rules for colocating data centers and large loads at power plants; existing PJM Tariff found 'unjust and unreasonable'; existing behind-the-meter generation rules 'no longer just and reasonable as applied to modern, large-scale co-located loads'; three new transmission services required (Firm Contract Demand, Non-Firm Contract Demand, Interim non-firm); PJM compliance filings on 20 January 2026 and 16 February 2026.
notes: STRUCTURAL ANCHOR — the canonical regulatory shift that institutionalises load-follows-generation. At 5 months, within the 6-month structural-anchor window.

title: Retirement delays of U.S. electric generating capacity may continue in 2026
key_claim: Owners planned to retire 12.3 GW in 2025 but retired only 4.6 GW, the least since 2008, after DOE emergency orders extended several coal plants. In 2026 6.4 GW of coal capacity (~4% of fleet) plus 4.6 GW of natural gas capacity scheduled to retire; multiple coal plant retirements (J.H. Campbell 1,331 MW, South Oak Creek 616 MW, R.M. Schahfer 722 MW, Craig Station 427 MW, Comanche 335 MW, F.B. Culley 90 MW) postponed from 2025 to 2026; further emergency orders could push 2026 retirements down again.
notes: Primary US government data on the coal retirement reversal. Hard quantification anchor.

title: The Interconnection Queue Continues to Be a Barrier to American Economic Competitiveness
key_claim: More than 2.2 TW of generation and storage projects in interconnection queues — nearly double installed grid capacity. Average time from interconnection request to commercial operation rose from <2 years in 2008 to nearly 5 years in 2024. Only 19% of projects requesting interconnection 2000-2019 had reached COD by end-2024. Co-locating generation and load reduces network upgrade costs; FERC's PJM order directs co-location rule development.
notes: Quality think-tank analysis on interconnection structural bottleneck. Tier 2 institutional.

title: Four Reasons New AI Data Centers Won't Overwhelm the Electricity Grid
key_claim: Hyperscalers know they must 'bring their own power' (BYOP) often by placing generating assets behind-the-meter. PJM capacity auction prices rose from ~$60/kWh in 2024 to >$300/kWh in 2025. Gas turbine prices up almost 200% since 2019. 240 GW of new US data center capacity announced for 2030 deployment (~20% of current US electricity demand). Only one-third of announced builds are actually being constructed. New data center deals fell >40% between Q3 and Q4 2025. Stargate appears to have stalled.
notes: COUNTER-SOURCE — the canonical institutional voice arguing the grid panic is overstated and the market is self-correcting via BYOP, demand management, and large-load tariffs. Used to anchor the counter-argument section.

title: FERC orders PJM to craft large load colocation rules
key_claim: FERC decision called 'major victory' for Constellation, PSEG, Vistra by Capstone analysts. FERC will consider minimum charge on colocated load to cover transmission system maintenance. FERC Commissioner Judy Chang concurred but flagged broader challenge of reliably integrating large loads and generation. FERC Chairman Laura Swett pledged consumer protection.
notes: Quality trade journalism on the December 2025 FERC order. Within 6-month structural anchor zone but the FERC fact sheet itself is the anchor; this is corroboration.

title: PJM proposes adding 14.9 GW with bilateral contracts, central procurement
key_claim: PJM proposing two-phase plan adding 14.9 GW: phase one would help match buyers (including data centers and large loads) with sellers of new generation; states and utilities may seek to lower the procurement target over affordability concerns. PJM testing central capacity procurement for the first time.
notes: April 2026 evidence that PJM is now actively brokering bespoke generation-to-load matches — operational evidence of the load-follows-generation shift.

title: Data center demand drives 66% surge in natural gas power plant costs
key_claim: BloombergNEF: cost to build a new combined-cycle gas turbine (CCGT) plant rose 66% in two years from <$1,500/kW in 2023 to $2,157/kW in 2025; construction time 23% longer. Gas turbine prices expected up 195% over 2019 by end-2026; waitlists into early 2030s. New US data center demand projected from 40 GW to 106 GW by 2035 (2.7x). Microsoft, Meta among tech companies building natural gas plants for data centers; Trump administration urged hyperscalers to 'bring their own power.'
notes: Anchor for the gas turbine supply-side bottleneck. Cites BloombergNEF and WoodMac. Quality tech journalism.
